notes: §1985:VII.2.7.3 SR2: "Data-name-1 may be qualified.", the one reference form §1985:III.2 lets the format's data-name take ("must not be reference-modified, subscripted, or qualified unless specifically permitted"). CapturePadding takes the word as data-name-1 through ClauseDataName (base name and IN/OF qualifiers; a subscript or reference modification is COBOL2024), ResolveFiles resolves it through ResolveClauseOperand with those qualifiers (COBOL1639 for an ambiguous, undefined or wrongly qualified name: the PB5070 fix), and ScreenPaddingDataName refuses an item under OCCURS, whose every reference must be subscripted (PB5499). Probes at 85 (work-rs-04/c2, c8): d) PC OF G2 OF H1, PC OF H1, PC IN G3, PC2 OF G1 and PC2 IN G1 run READ ABCD; b) unqualified PC2 and PC OF G2 (two matches) COBOL1639, PC OF G2 OF H9, PC OF G9 OF H1, PC2 OF G9 and an undefined name COBOL1639, PT (1), PC1 (1:1) and PL (1:1) COBOL2024; a) an unsubscripted OCCURS item COBOL6848; c/e/f do not reach a qualified-name operand (the clause is inert, GR2). The witness names PAD-CHAR OF PAD-GROUP-A where two groups define PAD-CHAR. next.reason: 1985 VII.2.7.3 SR2: PADDING CHARACTER 'Data-name-1 may be qualified.' The PADDING CHARACTER clause does not exist in 2023: the file control entry formats and clauses of §2023:12.4.5 contain no PADDING clause and the word PADDING is not a 2023 reserved word (deleted by the 2014 edition, docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.20). With the clause gone, the rule on its operand has no 2023 counterpart.
